_notes: Configured June 2026. Standard BigCommerce theme (ul.productGrid, h1.page-heading). No SearchSpring — native BC sort/search. Native BC search always returns results (full catalog for any term) — no zero-result state. Quote-only catalog (no prices, no cart, no qty input, no lead-time). Mobile nav is #mySidenav. Mobile breadcrumbs hidden. Footer root is plain <footer> (no .tcsFooter). No .Contact-info-box — contact info in footer .box:last-child. No payment icons. PLP at /aluminum/. Sidebar is .sidebarBlock. No subcategory tiles. PDP: no qty steppers, no carousel, no Yotpo, no SS recently-viewed. KNOWN SITE DEFICIENCY (test intentionally failing): products have no SKU set in BigCommerce admin — seo.cy.js JSON-LD Product block test fails. BRH admin must add SKUs (model numbers) to products. KNOWN SITE DEFICIENCY (test intentionally failing, verified July 28 2026 via direct HTML fetch): 2 of 15 pdp.popular products carry no spec-sheet PDF — /4-0-x-4-0-ee-single-leaf-roof-hatch-galvanized-steel-cover-and-curb-milcor/ and /24-x-38-fixed-deck-mounted-skylight-laminated-glass-fakro/ (the other 13 each have 1 PDF), so pdp.cy.js 'spec sheet links open PDFs in a new tab' (requires >=1 .pdf per PDP) fails ~13% of runs when the random pick lands on one — same deficiency class as CAD. This only became visible once the theme-error wrap let pdp.cy.js run past before-all. BRH admin must upload the manufacturer spec sheets for those 2 products in BigCommerce admin. Do NOT pin/exclude them from pdp.popular — that would mask the gap (site-deficiency policy). LIGHTHOUSE (calibrated July 2 2026, live scores homepage a11y 85 / plp 86 / pdp 79): all clear the fleet-wide accessibility:60 floor (no per-store override). KNOWN DEFICIENCY: homepage performance scored 42 vs the 50 floor (heavy content, fixable, not theme-structural) -> homepage Lighthouse test intentionally left failing; BRH devs must reduce homepage weight. KNOWN THEME BUGS (verified July 27-28 2026): the theme has MULTIPLE first-party bugs in its jQuery document-ready callbacks that throw on BRH pages (they fire for real users too): (1) heading-iteration JS calls .trim() on an undefined value ('Cannot read properties of undefined (reading trim)'), and (2) a ready callback calls $(...) when $ is not a function ('$ is not a function'). jQuery processes .ready()/Deferred callbacks asynchronously via window.setTimeout, and a throw inside one propagates out of that timer as an uncaught error that — confirmed live over several runs — never reaches the uncaught:exception handler in any suppressible way (not by message, not by stack, not via a capture-phase error listener). So they are prevented at the source: e2e.js registers a Cypress.on('window:before:load') that wraps the BRH window's setTimeout and swallows any throw whose stack shows the jQuery+bestroofhatches.com ready channel (code.jquery.com frames AND a bestroofhatches.com theme-callback frame). This is scoped by stack to exactly that channel, so it covers trim, '$ is not a function', and any further ready-callback bug in this theme without masking unrelated errors — and it lets the PDP/discovery/images suites actually run their assertions instead of dying in before-all. Temporary; BRH devs must fix the theme's document-ready scripts, then remove the wrap. Note: these surfaced only because commit d05ca7a replaced the old blanket uncaught:exception () => false (which swallowed everything) with a scoped handler; BRH ran 'green' before only because the blanket handler hid them. Also: Klaviyo email-capture popup is loaded (store-functional) and its telemetry fetch fails under Cypress, throwing an unhandled 'Failed to fetch' rejection → suppressed as third-party noise via KNOWN_BUGGY_SCRIPTS messagePattern /Failed to fetch/ (matched by message not stack because a fetch-rejection TypeError has a frameless stack in Chrome) + DEFAULT_IGNORE 'klaviyo' for the console-spy line (checks.js). Also: 1.door-pay.com tax-exempt form widget (bc_tax_exempt_form_load.js) throws 'setting hostUrl' on every BRH page load and is now blocked via THIRD_PARTY_HOSTS (door-pay.com) — vendor script bug, not ours. SEPT 29 2026: the taxonomy is NOT flat (the June 2026 _absentFeatures entry was stale and has been removed). plp.subcategory is /aluminum/babcock-davis/ — a child of plp.main /aluminum/, 15 products, h1 'Babcock Davis', trail Home > Aluminum > Babcock Davis (so the 'Aluminum' breadcrumbLabel is present), .sidebarBlock sidebar. Enables plp.cy.js's subcategory suite. pdp.mobileBreadcrumbsHidden now applies to phones only (trail renders at the 810px tablet). CHECKOUT (onboarded Sept 30 2026): the catalog is NOT purchase-free — pdp.popular is quote-only, but priced, cart-able hatches exist (five supplied by the store owner). checkout.product is /30-x-36-galvanized-steel-single-leaf-hatch-milcor/ (product id 3373, SKU BRH-M-1 3501-501-9, $1,264.53), purchasable, in stock, 0 attribute[] inputs; of the five, the two Elmdor hatches carry 2 required option groups each and were rejected. It ships FREIGHT only: 7 freight methods quote for the Houston persona, and the spec takes the first (Commercial - Freight Shipping, $495). DELIVERY AVAILABILITY: GET /api/storefront/form-fields reports field_28 as required:false, but BRH’s own inline /checkout script (FREIGHT_KEYWORDS = [freight]) moves the field_28 input below the shipping options and blocks #checkout-shipping-continue with ‘This field is required for freight shipping.’ whenever a freight method is selected — so customFields fills it as text (value in the store’s own placeholder format). Without it the step never collapses and assertShippingSummary() times out after 30s. activeStepClass is checkout-step--current (confirmed by dumping every step className). STORE CREDIT DOES NOT COVER THE ORDER: $234.24 is applied against a 1904.70 grand total (subtotal 1264.53 + shipping 495 + tax 145.17), leaving 1670.46 outstanding — harmless for the stop-at-payment test, but placeOrder must never be set here without funding the account first. The same stopFunction2 recursion as ADAP/FSE is present in the template (line 1029) but never fired across 4 runs: BRH offers only Stripe Checkout Session + Google Pay, so no empty .paymentProviderHeader-cc renders to trigger it. ‘Save this address’ ships CHECKED; the address book held 1 across four runs. Note these hatches now carry SKUs, so the ‘no SKU’ JSON-LD deficiency above may be worth re-verifying.
